Hey there /v/bodyweightfitness subscribers, today I'd like to share with you the single best technique I've ever found to bring up a lagging body part. It uses a very old and highly misunderstood concept called muscle control, which I'm sure you've at least passingly heard of, and it requires no change in your routine or extra exercises other than some added flexing in the mirror sessions throughout the day [which I'm sure most of you were already doing anyways] and some extra attentiveness during certain exercises.

I've used this method before to improve my glutes and my lats, and I'm currently using it to bring up my upper chest. I can assure you, from experience, that this works. Whether you have a Hank Hill ass, or Eugen Sandow pecs, or whatever else, this will help you bring your physique up to snuff.

Okay, so on to how to do it. There's really only two steps to this. The first step is to practice flexing whatever body part it is you're trying to improve in the mirror, at least twice a day for three to five flexes per session. This will help you to build awareness of, and control in, the muscle [thus, muscle control] and to help you better utilize it in the exercises it is supposed to be used in. Hold the flexes for three to five seconds apiece. Don't worry, this won't wear you out or negatively affect your workouts in any way at all.

The second step is to be extra conscientious of the muscle in whatever movements it is you are using to work it. If the body part is your chest, pay attention to it during your pushups, dips, and pec flies. If it's your glutes, focus on them in your pistol squats, shrimp squats, and glute-ham raises. Basically, make sure that the muscle is doing it's fair share of the work in all of the movements it is meant to be a prime mover in.

One more thing, if you are having a hard time learning to really squeeze and flex the muscle, either independently in flexing sessions or in combination with other muscles during your workouts, look up the purpose of the muscle in an anatomy textbook or on google. For example, the quadriceps' main purpose is to extend the knee. Knowing this will greatly help you in your control of the muscle as it will give you something concrete to focus on.

And there you have it. That's really all there is to it. Using this method, you can bring up any lagging body part, without adding needless ancillary movements to your routine, inside of two to three months, assuming you are eating at at least maintenance level. I wouldn't recommend trying this on a cut as it's not likely to do much, as on a cut you are in an overall catabolic state and can't put on much muscle. Just wait until after your cut is over and do it then.

Doing this multiple times over the years with multiple bodyparts plays a key role in improving your body awareness, and can help you achieve not only your optimal physique, but your maximum strength through maximum contraction of every possible muscle in every movement.

Best of luck to everyone.

-Demonic_Mime
